name: Deleted subject
what: leaves an actor unstated within the matched construction
affordance: can background agency or foreground an event when the actor is unknown, irrelevant, or strategically omitted
mechanism: agent deletion via passive/non-agentive framing; measurably shifts blame and damages (Fausey & Boroditsky 2010: agentive framing produced 53% higher fines)
benign_reading: Passives are often just information structure, and in pro-drop languages (Chinese, Japanese, Spanish) subjectless sentences are the unmarked default — detection logic must key on agency-at-issue, not subject absence. English-only logic inverts elsewhere.
ledger_line: {n} construction{s} with the actor unstated in the matched span
output_phrasing: this construction leaves the actor unstated within the matched span

naming_events.source: Arabic grammatical tradition; rhetorically motivated ellipsis (ḥadhf) theorized by al-Jurjānī, Dalā'il al-I'jāz

Schneider/Safire, on 'mistakes were made' (Grant 1876 → Ziegler 1973 → Reagan 1987)

specimens.speaker: Ronald Reagan
specimens.note: State of the Union on Iran-Contra: the passive deletes the maker of the mistakes — his own administration and himself — acknowledging failure while the grammar leaves no one to blame (Safire's canonical 'past exonerat…

specimens.quote: no one is blameless here; it costs so much money to pay for these campaigns, that mistakes were made here by people who either did it deliberately or inadvertently
specimens.speaker: Bill Clinton
specimens.note: News conference on Democratic fundraising: the nominal agent is an indefinite crowd ('people who either did it deliberately or inadvertently'), so the passive diffuses responsibility from the White House to everyone a…

specimens.quote: Approximately 40 million credit and debit card accounts may have been impacted between Nov. 27 and Dec. 15, 2013.
specimens.speaker: Target Corporation
specimens.note: Breach announcement: accounts arrive pre-'impacted' as if by weather — the grammar deletes both the criminals who stole the card data and Target's own custodial failure to secure it.

specimens.quote: As a result of the incident, OPM will send notifications to approximately 4 million individuals whose PII may have been compromised.
specimens.speaker: U.S. Office of Personnel Management
specimens.note: Federal breach notice: PII 'may have been compromised' with no grammatical actor — neither the intruders nor the agency whose unmodernized systems let them in appear as the subject of any failure.

specimens.quote: In addition, credit card numbers for approximately 209,000 U.S. consumers, and certain dispute documents with personal identifying information for approximately 182,000 U.S. consumers, were accessed.
specimens.speaker: Equifax Inc.
specimens.note: Breach press release (also SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1): the sentence detailing the worst data loss ends in an agentless 'were accessed,' deleting both the criminals and Equifax's unpatched web application that admitted them.

honest_twins.text: It was decided — unanimously, by all nine of us at Tuesday's meeting — that club dues would stay at ten dollars.
honest_twins.note: Contains the surface pattern 'it was decided,' but the deciders are named in the same clause ('by all nine of us'), so no agency is hidden; the passive is pure information structure, foregrounding the decision readers care about — exactly the entry's benign_reading (agency is not at issue).

honest_twins.text: All evening flights were delayed by the thunderstorm; gate agents rebooked every passenger overnight.
honest_twins.note: Matches the entry regex ('were delayed'), but the cause sits openly in the by-phrase and is a natural event with no responsible agent to conceal; the passive simply fronts what the reader needs (their flight), so the benign_reading — information structure, not blame diffusion — applies.
